description:
An inbox fills up whether you look at it or not. Receipts, boarding passes, GitHub alerts, newsletters, sales, and the odd scam, all in one pile.

Hagaki reads your inbox and files it into seven folders: Receipts, Travel, Dev, Newsletters, Social, Promotions and Junk. In Gmail they are labels. In iCloud Mail they are folders. Mail from real people stays in your inbox.

Nothing is deleted. Filing moves mail out of the inbox and into its box, and junk gets a box too. Delete is a separate button. The list is a preview first, and nothing moves until you tap File everything.

Junk is scored on real signals: a sender name that does not match its domain, urgency language, an unsubscribe header from a stranger. Unsubscribe sends the sender's own one-click request where they support it.

Connect Gmail or iCloud Mail, or try the demo inbox with sample mail and no account. Outlook is not supported yet.

Hagaki (葉書) is Japanese for postcard. Every Japanese postcard has seven red boxes for the postal code, so machines can sort the mail. Hagaki sorts your inbox the same way.
promotionalText: Seven smart folders for your inbox. Nothing is deleted. People stay put.
